Getting paid often means typing out the same block of details over and over. Bank name, account number, IFSC, UPI ID, maybe a PayPal address for overseas clients. You paste it into a chat, it wraps awkwardly, someone mistypes a digit, and the payment goes sideways.
A payment card generator turns that messy block into one tidy, shareable card. Add your payment methods, pick a look, and share it as an image or copy it as clean text. Everything runs in your browser, so your details stay yours.
👉 Open the Free Payment Card Generator
What You Can Build
The idea is simple: one card that holds all the ways someone can pay you. You give it a title, choose a theme, and add as many payment methods as you need.
Supported methods include:

• Bank Transfer — account details, IFSC, and more

• PayPal — for international clients

• UPI — for quick payments in India

• Wise — for low-fee cross-border transfers

• Western Union — for cash-style transfers

• Crypto wallets — for those who pay in digital currency
Add a note if you need to (like “please mention your name in the reference”), and you’re done.
Six Themes to Match Your Style
The card isn’t just functional, it looks the part. Pick from six themes:
Classic, Dark, Ocean, Forest, Royal, and Sunset.
A freelancer sending a card to a client, a small business adding payment details to an invoice, a creator sharing donation options, the right theme makes it look intentional rather than thrown together.
How to Make Your Card

• Open the Payment Card Generator

• Give it a Card Title (e.g. “Payment Details — Your Name”)

• Choose a theme

• Under Add Payment Methods, pick a method, fill in the details, and click Add, repeat for as many as you like

• Add an optional note

• Download it as an image or copy it as text
That’s the whole process. No account, no waiting.
Where a Payment Card Actually Helps

• Freelancers — send clients one clean card instead of a wall of text

• Small businesses — attach payment options to invoices or emails

• Creators — share tip or donation methods with your audience

• Sellers — give buyers a clear, professional way to pay

• Anyone splitting a bill — share your UPI or bank details without the back-and-forth
Why It Beats Pasting Raw Text
Copy-pasting bank details into a chat works, technically. But it’s easy to misread, it wraps badly on phones, and it looks unprofessional. A generated card lays everything out cleanly, keeps the numbers aligned, and, as an image, it’s harder to mistype because the reader can see it clearly rather than squinting at run-together text.
For freelancers and small businesses especially, a tidy payment card sends a small signal that you’re organised, which is never a bad thing when you’re asking to be paid.
A Word on Safety
This is worth being clear about. A payment card is meant for details you’re comfortable sharing with people paying you, things like your UPI ID, PayPal address, or the account number and IFSC you’d put on an invoice anyway.
A few sensible habits:

• Only include what’s needed for someone to send you money. You rarely need to share more than the basics.

• Never put sensitive card data on it, like your debit/credit card’s full number, CVV, or PIN. Those are for you to enter when you pay, never to share.

• Share it with people you’re actually transacting with, not publicly, unless it’s a genuine donation or tip card you intend for the world to see.
Used sensibly, it’s just a neater version of the details you’d hand over anyway.
Getting the Best Result

• Title it clearly with your name, so the payer knows whose account they’re sending to.

• Double-check every digit before you share, one wrong number in an account or UPI ID sends money nowhere.

• Add a reference note so incoming payments are easy to match to the right person or invoice.

• Pick a readable theme if the card will be viewed on small screens, high contrast helps.
Privacy
The card is built entirely in your browser. Nothing you type, your bank details, UPI ID, wallet addresses, is uploaded or stored anywhere. It stays on your device, and once you close the tab, it’s gone. You’re the only one who ever sees what you enter here.
Common Questions
Is it free? Yes, completely free. No Pro version, no signup, no limits. Create and download as many payment cards as you want without paying anything or making an account.
Is it safe to enter my bank details? The tool builds the card entirely in your browser and never uploads or stores anything, so your details stay private. Only include information you’d normally share to receive a payment, never sensitive data like a card CVV or PIN.
Can I add multiple payment methods to one card? Yes. Add as many as you like, bank transfer, PayPal, UPI, Wise, Western Union, crypto, and they’ll all appear together on the same card.
Can I download the card? Yes. You can download it as an image to share anywhere, or copy the details as plain text if you prefer to paste them.
